summary: Intermittent duplicate/ghost candidates and elevated tail latency from reranker after embedding replication lag
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report intermittent duplicate or 'ghost' candidates in rerank responses along with spikes in 95/99th percentile latency on the rerank endpoint. The behavior started around 2026-03-05 09:10 UTC and has been seen only in eu-west production.

Impact:
- Some queries return duplicate candidate IDs or stale results that were recently deleted/updated in the corpus.
- Rerank tail latency increases (p95 -> 2x, p99 -> 3-4x) during incidents, causing timeouts for downstream application flows.
- Affects HalcyonSearch internal users and their end-customers; business-critical search experiences are degraded.

Environment:
- Prod, eu-west region
- Customer uses enterprise account with dedicated indexing pipeline and alias routing to redwood-reranker-v1.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Submit large batch similarity request (500 candidate prefilter) against rerank endpoint with user alias X.
2) Occasionally response includes duplicate candidate IDs and rerank returns subset with high latency or 504s.
3) Re-run same query after 10-30s often returns expected results.

Logs/observations:
- Reranker logs occasionally show "lookup miss -> fallback_merge" entries and then duplicate merges.
- Ingest consumer lag spikes observed in the embedding-ingest consumer group (Kinesis/consumer lag ~ 3-8 minutes during event window).
- Index shard reassign events recorded at 2026-03-05T09:08:45Z in cluster controller logs.
- No config rollouts were published in the 24h prior.

Customer notes:
- Customer team observed duplicate IDs that should have been removed by a delete pipeline. They believe deletions had been applied upstream but reranker still returned deleted documents intermittently.
comments: [2026-03-05] Customer (HalcyonSearch) - We started seeing duplicates and occasional timeouts around 09:10 UTC. Deletions were applied earlier this morning; can you confirm consistency?
[2026-03-05] Support (Aisha Khan) - Acknowledged. Creating ticket and escalating to SRE/Indexing. Can you share an example query and a candidate ID that should be deleted?
[2026-03-05] Customer (HalcyonSearch) - Provided example query id=qs-77 and candidate id=doc-2456. Attaching request payload and a later response where doc-2456 still appears.

[2026-03-05] SRE (Miguel Ortega) - Observed consumer lag on embedding-ingest group in eu-west coincident with shard reassignment events. Rebalancer ran and a few replicas were rehomed. Investigating whether rebalancer applied before delete tombstones propagated.

[2026-03-06] Eng (Nina Patel) - We've reproduced duplicate candidate behavior in a replay test where ingestion and index-rebalance overlapped. Hypothesis: stale replica served reads while delete tombstones were still in flight causing temporary re-appearance. Working on a mitigation to pin read replicas during shard moves.
[2026-03-07] Support (Aisha Khan) - Temporary mitigation applied: restarted one ingest consumer to speed catch-up and enabled a short read-consistency gate for alias X. Asking customer to monitor.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Timeline: 2026-03-05 09:06 UTC cluster controller triggered shard reassign; at 09:08 UTC embedding-ingest consumer lag increased due to GC pauses on a single host.
- Root cause hypothesis: race between index shard reassign and delayed ingestion consumer -> tombstones (deletes) had not replicated to the replica that served the rerank read, producing ghost candidates.
- Evidence: consumer lag metrics (Grafana dashboard 'ingest.consumer.lag' spike), controller logs showing 'reassign start' / 'reassign complete' around same window, reranker access logs showing reads from replica-3 which had older watermark.
- Also saw increased pushback from router when reranker cache invalidation failed, which prolonged stale reads.
- Reproduction: integration replay with artificial consumer lag + simulated shard move reproduces duplicates and p99 latency spikes.
- Links: Grafana panels - https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/consumer-lag-eu-west (time window 2026-03-05 08:50-09:20), Cluster controller logs - https://logs.redwood.ai/query?range=2026-03-05T09:00/2026-03-05T09:20
resolution:
Mitigations and next steps applied:
1) Immediate: restarted affected ingest consumer and forced a catch-up; enabled alias-level read-consistency gate for HalcyonSearch for 1 hour to prevent reads from replicas during replication catch-up. This brought p95/p99 back near baseline.
2) Short-term: deployed a conservative rebalancer throttle so shard reassigns do not overlap with consumer catch-up windows; added a guard to delay serving from a replica until its watermark >= leader watermark for alias-specific shards.
3) Long-term: planned changes - (a) stronger tombstone propagation guarantees via commit-ack semantics for deletes, (b) improved observability for per-alias replication watermarks, (c) postmortem scheduled.
4) Customer follow-up: Completed a scoped backfill to purge ghost candidates from the affected replica and validated results with HalcyonSearch prior to closing.

Status: mitigation in place, working on long-term fixes. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-12.
follow_up_actions: Implement replica watermark check before serving reads (owner: SRE team, target 2026-03-20)
Add Grafana alert for alias-level replication lag > 2m (owner: Observability, target 2026-03-10)
Customer check-in call scheduled 2026-03-09 to review actions and closure (owner: CSM - Jordan Li)
